what_happened: At Sri's request, the the person running Athena hand-edited athena.toml and raised the time limits for reader, planner, critic, producer and verifier to 86400 s. The check timeout went to 14400 s as a hung-test guard. The reason was that six jobs since 13 Nov evening failed when the planner, escalated to xhigh effort on revision rounds, hit its 600 s limit. No job was involved, and the event is logged as an intervention. The aim is to measure how long things take and why.
cause: The planner's time limit was a fixed number that was never compared with measured planner durations. The planner's effort level rises on revision rounds, so its runtime grows, and nothing adjusted the limit to match. Athena records no per-stage timing against limits and does not tell a timeout from a real failure. Repeated deadline stops therefore piled up as failed jobs, and a person had to remove every limit by hand.
other_causes: No partial plan or progress signal is kept when the planner times out, so six jobs lost their planning work.
The change removes the limits for five roles at once, so a hung agent can now run up to a day and spend money. Only the check timeout keeps a guard.
open_hypotheses: The input does not show whether the planner was slow because of xhigh effort, plan size, or the planner stalling.
The input does not show whether the other roles (reader, critic, producer, verifier) were near their limits; they were raised along with the planner as a precaution.
Whether the budget cost caps still bound a runaway agent once the time limits are gone is not stated.
contradictions: The event raised the limits for every role, but only the planner limit is cited as failing. The other roles show no failures in this event.
The case is filed under a planner-deadline class, but the fix is a manual config edit that sets the limit to a day, so it is also like the earlier verifier-limit case.
prevention: Athena should record each stage's elapsed time against its limit for every job. It should report any stage that finishes over about 70% of its limit. It should record a deadline stop as a timeout, separate from a real failure, with the partial output kept, so a person can see the cause. A raised effort level on revision rounds should come with a matching time budget. Where limits are removed, a high safety ceiling and the cost cap should stay in place to bound runaway runs.
proposed_request: Add per-stage timing to Athena. For every job, record how long the reader, planner, critic, producer, verifier and checks each took, the planner's effort level on each round, and the configured limit. Show these in `athena status` and in a timing report per job. When a stage hits its deadline, record it as a timeout, not as a job failure, and keep any partial plan or output. Add a warning when a stage ends above 70% of its limit. Acceptance: (1) run on the last six jobs that failed at the planner limit and show the real planner duration per round with its effort level; (2) a test shows a timed-out planner leaves a timeout record with the partial plan kept; (3) a test shows the warning appears over 70% of the limit; (4) add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
